common.keysHint: Keyboard: arrows move aim · Space/E select
common.o2Out: You ran out of oxygen mid-task.

roca.title: Rock Core
roca.objective: Goal: a layered SEDIMENTARY rock formed in the water of Jezero's ancient lake.
roca.instScan: Sweep the scanner (or arrow keys) over each rock to clear dust and read it. Then pick one.
roca.pickFirst: Tap a scanned rock first to select it.

leopard.name: Sedimentary · layers & spots
leopard.read: Layers: YES · Origin: lake · Spots: YES

sandstone.name: Loose sandstone
sandstone.read: Layers: NO · Loose grains that crumble

volcanic.name: Volcanic basalt
volcanic.read: Layers: NO · Origin: lava, no water

roca.wrongRock: That rock didn't form in water: it holds no record of the ancient lake.
roca.wrongRockFail: You drilled rocks that can't answer the science question. Every tube counts: Perseverance only carries 43.
roca.instTrivia: NASA Question (1, 2, or 3): answer right for +5 science pts before drilling.
roca.triviaWrong: Not quite—check the real fact below.

trivia.q: In July 2024 Perseverance found 'leopard spots' on Cheyava Falls. Which crater was it exploring?
trivia.fact: Jezero spans 45 km and held a river and lake around 3.5 billion years ago. Source: NASA JPL (2024).

trivia.q: According to NASA's study (Nature, 2025), what minerals form the rims of those spots?
trivia.fact: Vivianite and greigite often form via chemical reactions involving organic matter in water. Source: NASA JPL (2025).

trivia.q: How many titanium tubes does the Perseverance rover carry to store Martian samples?
trivia.fact: Perseverance carries 43 tubes; Sapphire Canyon (at Cheyava Falls) was rock core #22. Source: NASA Mars 2020 (JPL).

roca.instDrill: Hold click (or Space/E) to drill. HARD layers heat the bit faster. Release to cool.
roca.overheat: Drill overheated and the core cracked! Back to the last safe layer.
roca.overheatFail: The core crumbled—just like Perseverance's first attempt at Roubion rock (August 2021): an empty tube.
roca.instSeal: Seal the tube: press Space/E or the button when the marker enters green.
roca.sealTwice: High difficulty: you need TWO seals in a row.
roca.sealMiss: Loose seal: Martian air would contaminate the sample.
roca.sealFail: The tube wasn't properly sealed. A contaminated core can't be used to search for signs of life.
roca.success: Core sealed! Sedimentary rocks preserve clues of ancient life. In July 2024 Perseverance found 'leopard spots' on Cheyava Falls—NASA called it the clearest potential biosignature yet in 2025.

suelo.title: Regolith Sample
suelo.objective: Goal: FINE dust. That's what gets into future astronauts' suits, joints, and lungs.
suelo.instScoop: Stop the scoop at the right amount (green zone): too little falls short, too much clogs the sieve.
suelo.instSieve: Shake ALTERNATING ◄ and ► (arrow keys). Tap large pebbles before they tear the mesh.
suelo.sameSide: Alternate sides so the grain doesn't clump.
suelo.pebbleTore: A pebble tore the sieve mesh!
suelo.instChoose: Check the scale on each jar and store the FINEST grain.
suelo.wrongJar: That grain is too coarse to study the dust astronauts would breathe.
suelo.fail: Without a fine sample we can't measure how dust harms spacesuits and lungs.
suelo.success: Regolith stored! In Dec 2022 Perseverance collected its first regolith samples to see how dust affects crews and hardware. Watch out: it contains perchlorates, toxic salts detected by Phoenix in 2008.

minerales.title: Vein Analysis
minerales.instTool: Read the objective and select the right instrument (1, 2, or 3).

objectives.organicos: Search for ORGANIC MOLECULES (carbon-based) inside the vein.
objectives.agua: Confirm HYDRATED MINERALS (water-bearing) inside the vein.
objectives.elementos: Measure which CHEMICAL ELEMENTS make up the rock.

sherloc.name: 1 SHERLOC
sherloc.desc: Ultraviolet laser: makes organic compounds glow

supercam.name: 2 SuperCam
supercam.desc: Laser + infrared light: detects water in minerals

minerales.wrongTool: Wrong instrument for that goal. Each laser pulse drains battery.
minerales.instExtract: Tap the vein nodes IN ORDER (1, 2, 3…) before the battery runs out.
minerales.instExtractMemory: Memorize the order: numbers fade quickly.
minerales.wrongNode: Wrong order: the mineral vein fractured slightly.
minerales.instSeal: Seal the fragment in the tube when the marker enters green.
minerales.fail: Analysis inconclusive. On Mars instruments have strict power and time budgets: every mistake costs.
minerales.success: Vein analyzed and sealed! Perseverance uses SHERLOC (UV) for organics, SuperCam (laser/IR) for water-bearing minerals, and PIXL (X-rays) for elements. Hydrated minerals prove Jezero held water.

aire.title: Atmosphere Sample
aire.objective: Goal: capture ~6 millibars of Martian air without contamination.
aire.instCouple: Turn the coupler: press Space/E or the button when the yellow notch points UP.
aire.coupleMiss: Misaligned coupler: dust got into the valve.
aire.instFill: Hold the valve (or Space/E) to raise pressure. Keep the needle in green to fill the bar. Watch for gusts!
aire.overPressure: Overpressure! The tube had to purge.
aire.instClose: Close NOW! Press Space/E or the button before pressure leaks.
aire.closeLate: Closed too late: the pressure escaped.
aire.fail: Air sample contaminated. Measuring the exact atmosphere helps explain how Mars lost most of its air.
aire.success: Air captured! ~95% CO₂, ~3% nitrogen, and 2% argon at only ~6 mbar (Earth is 1,013). Fun fact: Perseverance's first core tube (Roubion, 2021) missed the rock—but brought back Martian air!

paneles.title: Clean Solar Panel
paneles.instBrush: Drag the brush (or arrows + Space) over the dust. Reach 90% clean before time runs out.
paneles.windHint: Wind blows dust back in: hurry!
paneles.timeOut: Time ran out and the panel is still dusty. Retrying with lower base power.
paneles.fail: The panel stayed coated. That's how InSight shut down in Dec 2022 when dust covered its arrays.
paneles.success: Panel spotless! Base energy will gradually recover. Dust silenced InSight in 2022; Spirit and Opportunity lasted for years thanks to lucky wind cleaning events.

tuberias.instRotate: Rotate pipe segments (click, or arrows + Space/E) to link IN and OUT. Then press Test (P).
tuberias.instClog: Segments marked ✕ are clogged: tap 3 times to clear them first.
tuberias.leak: Leak! Flow stops where the connection breaks.
tuberias.clogged: Clogged segment: clear it before rotating.
tuberias.soxeInst: Heat the SOXE stack (Space/E or button) near 800 °C to split CO₂ into O₂ without overheating.
tuberias.soxeOverheatFail: SOXE reactor thermal runaway! Emergency cooldown triggered.
tuberias.failMoxie: Leaks or thermal stress damaged the stack. Without MOXIE, base oxygen drops every hour.
tuberias.failAntenna: Antenna still offline. Without it, solar storm alerts from Earth can't arrive.
tuberias.successMoxie: MOXIE online! Between 2021 and 2023 it produced 122 g of O₂ from Martian CO₂ at ~800 °C—proving future crews can breathe and refuel on Mars.
tuberias.successAntenna: Antenna aligned! Rovers communicate with Earth directly or via orbiters like MRO, heard by giant dishes of NASA's Deep Space Network.
